title: Forget Bloat: Northstar is the Browser Built from Scratch You Need to See!
contentMarkdown:
## 📝 Quick Summary: 
Northstar is a minimalist, independent web browser written in C, designed for Linux, macOS, and Windows. It aims for modern web standards compatibility without relying on existing browser engines like Gecko or WebKit, focusing on security and a lean architecture.

## 🔑 Key Takeaways

- ✅ Northstar is a minimalist web browser written entirely in C, from scratch.

- ✅ It features a custom engine supporting modern HTML5, CSS, and JavaScript without embedding large existing engines.

- ✅ Prioritizes security with sandboxing, seccomp filters, and no JIT compilation.

- ✅ Offers a compact, auditable codebase (approx. 177k lines of C) for transparency and efficiency.

- ✅ Supports key web standards like Service Workers, WebExtensions, IndexedDB, and WebSockets, making it surprisingly capable.


## 📊 Project Statistics
- ⭐ Stars: 86
- 🍴 Forks: 6
- ❗ Open Issues: 3


## 🛠 Tech Stack
- ✅ C


Hey fellow developers! Ever felt like modern web browsers are just getting heavier, slower, and more complex? Do you dream of a browser that's lean, mean, and built with security and simplicity at its core? Well, clear your schedules, because I've stumbled upon a GitHub project that's absolutely blowing my mind, and I think you'll feel the same. Meet Northstar, a web browser crafted from the ground up in pure C, and it's a game-changer!What makes Northstar so special? It's not just another wrapper around existing engines like WebKit or Blink. Nope, this is a true "from scratch" endeavor, with its own engine meticulously designed to tackle practical HTML5, modern CSS, and JavaScript compatibility. Imagine the sheer engineering feat! This isn't just a hobby project; it's a serious attempt to build a robust, standards-compliant browser without the massive overhead typically associated with them. It's available for Linux, macOS, and Windows, so everyone can get a taste of this marvel.The philosophy behind Northstar is pure minimalism. Forget tabs, multiple renderer processes, or fancy (and often unnecessary) features like WebGL, WebGPU, or embedded PDF viewers. Northstar opts for a single page per window, a single process, and an architecture where the GTK shell runs on the main thread while the page engine handles rendering on a dedicated thread. This means a slow page won't freeze your entire window – a brilliant design choice for responsiveness. The entire engine is a compact body of C code, roughly 177,000 lines. This small footprint is a huge deal because it makes the entire browser auditable by a single person, enhancing transparency and trust.But don't let the "minimalist" tag fool you into thinking it's basic. Northstar supports a surprising array of modern web standards. We're talking HTML parsing via lexbor, a custom-built CSS cascade that handles flex, grid, transforms, and animations, and JavaScript powered by the QuickJS interpreter, complete with DOM, Shadow DOM, Canvas 2D, and WebCrypto. It even includes support for custom elements, dedicated workers, IndexedDB (backed by SQLite), WebSockets, and perhaps most excitingly for many of us, Service Workers and WebExtensions! Yes, you can run your beloved browser extensions and build offline-first experiences.Security is another area where Northstar shines. On Linux, it runs behind a Landland filesystem sandbox and uses a default-deny seccomp syscall filter, both in GUI and headless modes. Plus, there's no JIT (Just-In-Time) compilation, which significantly reduces the attack surface. For developers, this means a more secure environment for browsing and a project that prioritizes safety from the ground up.So, why should you check this out? If you're tired of resource-hungry browsers, if you value security and auditability, or if you're just fascinated by the inner workings of web technology, Northstar offers an unparalleled opportunity. It's a fantastic learning resource for understanding browser internals, and it could be perfect for specialized applications, embedded systems, or anyone who wants a fast, secure, and bloat-free browsing experience. This project isn't just cool; it's a testament to what's possible when you rethink fundamental tools. Dive in, explore the code, and maybe even contribute to this incredible journey!
